about.title: Tiburon Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Tiburon is a small, close-knit community, and a workplace injury here can feel especially disruptive when your job, your commute, and your daily routine are all tied to the same few corridors — Tiburon Boulevard, Paradise Drive, Cecilia Way, and Rt 131. Whether you work at a marina, a restaurant, a retail shop, a construction site, or you drive for work along these roads, California law generally requires injured workers to go through workers' compensation first, regardless of who was at fault. But that's not always the end of the story. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, you may also have a separate third-party claim worth pursuing. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise outcomes — we simply connect injured workers in Tiburon with an independent attorney who can look at the specifics of your case, explain your options plainly, and help you understand the next step forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your Tiburon Workplace Injury

items.title: Workers' Comp Isn't Always the Whole Picture
items.desc: California treats workers' compensation as the usual remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party — like a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment maker — can still be separately liable. An attorney can help sort out whether that applies to your situation.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter
items.desc: You generally need to report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, and missing that window can complicate your claim. Getting guidance early helps make sure you don't lose options by waiting too long.

items.title: Retaliation Is Against the Law
items.desc: It's illegal for an employer to punish you for reporting an injury or filing a claim. If you're worried about how reporting might affect your job, an independent attorney can explain your protections.

items.question: I was hurt at a job in Tiburon — do I have to go through workers' comp, or can I sue?
items.answer: In most cases, workers' compensation is the exclusive remedy against your employer, meaning you generally can't sue your employer directly even if they were careless. However, if a third party outside your employer — like another driver on Tiburon Boulevard or a piece of defective equipment — contributed to your injury, you may have a separate claim worth exploring.

items.question: What if my injury happened while driving for work near Paradise Drive or Cecilia Way?
items.answer: If you were injured in a work-related vehicle incident on local roads like Paradise Drive or Cecilia Way, you may have both a workers' comp claim and a potential third-party claim against another driver. An independent attorney can review the details and explain how the two interact.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim if a third party was involved?
items.answer: Third-party injury claims in California generally carry a two-year deadline from the date of injury. That's separate from the 30-day window for reporting the injury to your employer, so it helps to get clarity on both timelines early.
